inputs.title: The Adventure Begins
inputs.logline: When eager young Keen sails away from home and into a sudden storm, he discovers that courage is not looking fearless — it is leaping to help a friend while the fear is still in his paws.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Tiny pollen sacks bounce on their back legs. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: At bee height in the flower field, Zenny’s graceful work is contrasted with Fuzzby’s full-throttle pollen chaos. His first crash into the leaf becomes his self-declared success, establishing that his comedy is not clumsiness alone but proud denial after impact.
beats.want: Fuzzby wants to look like a competent, important pollen collector.
beats.need: He needs to know he belongs even when his body betrays the performance.
beats.kidRead: Funny bee zooms, bonks, bounces back, and acts like it was perfect.
beats.adultRead: The anxious little performer is already covering failure with dignity; the laugh comes from recognition, not humiliation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Open with buoyant safety and instant character contrast, making the world playful before any storm threat enters.

vision.premise: Keen leaves home for Crystal Cove, carrying his father’s empty wristbands and a brave face that keeps wobbling. A storm separates him from safety, but when Squeaky is trapped, Keen acts before he feels ready — and earns both his Aquamarine crystal and a new family.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen stop performing bravery long enough to discover the real thing inside him — and can home let him go without disappearing from him?
vision.theme: You can be afraid and brave at the same time; the scared part is where the brave part begins.
vision.externalJourney: Keen departs the pier, sails into open water, loses his map in a storm, follows Squeaky, dives into dangerous water to free him, reaches Crystal Cove, and is welcomed into the Crystal Bears.
vision.internalJourney: Keen begins by trying to look ready. Each wobble exposes the truth he is hiding: he is excited, nervous, and carrying his father’s memory. Underwater, with no audience to impress, he chooses someone else’s safety over his own fear. By the end, his confidence is no longer a performance; it has a home.
vision.relationshipChanges: Keen and his Mum shift from protected cub and holding parent to trusted traveler and mother who lets go. Keen and Squeaky become playmates through rescue and mutual saving. Aida moves from distant witness to welcoming elder. The bears shift from rescuers on the shore to Keen’s new found family. Fuzzby immediately adopts Keen as a heroic honey-friend, with Zenny quietly managing the chaos.
vision.emotionalCurve: Warm golden departure, comic bravado, ache of goodbye, stormy isolation, underwater nadir, fierce selfless action, relieved laughter, communal welcome, and a settled golden-hour belonging that still remembers the goodbye.
vision.comedyCurve: Fuzzby’s chaotic pollen incompetence opens the episode with character comedy, then Keen inherits the same cover-up shape with his boat wobble. Squeaky adds misunderstanding play. Fuzzby’s emergency panic and later hero-worship keep the rescue from becoming too heavy. The honey button releases the final ache without erasing it.
vision.setupPayoffMap: Fuzzby’s ‘meant to do that’ bravado sets up Keen’s similar wobble cover. The pollen-field thunder sets up the storm. Aida’s vision sets up Keen’s departure. Mum’s empty wristbands set up their faint underwater glow and later the Aquamarine gems settling into them. Squeaky’s playful introduction sets up his later danger and rescue. Mum’s promise that Keen will not be alone is paid off by Aida’s message home and the family welcome.
vision.visualMotifs: Empty gold wristbands becoming light-bearing wristbands; tiny figures against widening water; hands closing and opening; warm home light giving way to cold storm blue, then returning as post-storm gold; Squeaky’s arcs through water; Fuzzby’s motion crashing against Zenny’s stillness; the final group moving as one along the shore.
vision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s manic buzz-crash rhythm; Zenny’s dry stillness after chaos; Aida’s rose-quartz bowl tone; distant wind growing into storm; Squeaky’s chirps shifting from play to distress to relief; Keen’s breath catching before brave action; Aquamarine’s B-note resolving into the group chord.
vision.climax: At the darkest underwater point, with Squeaky trapped and a massive wave gathering above, Keen’s vacant wristbands glow from within as he braces, pulls with everything he has, tears the net free, and is thrown into the storm water before Squeaky carries him back toward the glowing shore.
vision.resolution: Aida awards Keen the Aquamarine, which splits into gems for his father’s wristbands, and the Crystal Bears embrace him as family. The episode ends not with triumph alone, but with golden-hour laughter, the shore calm again, and Keen walking with new friends while home is still emotionally present.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, relieved, funny, and a little tearful — the feeling of watching a child step into the world and find that love followed them there.

treatments.name: Fuzzby’s Uncatchable Parade
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience is invited to ride the first minute like a tiny, joyful bee-rollercoaster: funny speed, soft danger, instant safety. Kids feel the zig-zag thrill and the bonk; adults read the little performer trying to convert every mistake into status before anyone can pity him.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene belongs to Fuzzby’s Want: to appear important, official, and in control. Zenny is the emotional truth sitting beside him: she does not punish the crash, she simply sees it. The thunder turn briefly shifts the emotional authority to Zenny, because she understands the world before he does.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: escalating overcommitment. Each Fuzzby correction becomes a bigger public ceremony of denial: the leaf impact becomes “Nailed it,” the pollen mess becomes rank, the attempted fix becomes a tumble, the storm becomes material for a boast. Secondary mechanism: movement against stillness, with Zenny’s economy making his excess funnier.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby never plays ‘clumsy’; he plays ‘senior pollen professional’ with total commitment. His body betrays the act first: erratic altitude, too much acceleration into flowers, chest-out recovery before balance has actually returned. His pride always arrives half a beat before his body is ready. Zenny’s performance is small, precise, and unhurried: eyes lead, body follows, smile rationed, laugh withheld until the chaos earns it. When thunder arrives, Fuzzby tries to annex it into the show; Zenny removes all extra motion and lets the warning land plainly.
treatments.visualGrammar: The frame is constantly being tugged by Fuzzby’s momentum and corrected by Zenny’s stillness. Flower stems become vertical lanes he cannot respect; petals become soft traps; leaves are spring-loaded witnesses. The visual joke is that the world is graceful until Fuzzby enters it, then every graceful object becomes an accomplice.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera follows Fuzzby as if it is one small bee behind him, often a breath late, letting him exceed the frame edge for comic danger. It abandons him decisively for Zenny whenever her still reaction is the punchline. When thunder interrupts, the camera stops chasing and lets the field itself feel suddenly larger than both bees.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Fuzzby supplies continuous unstable movement: fast, porpoising, oversteering, recovering too proudly. Zenny supplies stillness with purpose: hovering smooth, holding eye contact, letting a blink or tiny mouth-corner shift do the work. The storm beat reverses the scene’s energy: Fuzzby keeps moving to deny fear, while Zenny’s stillness becomes alertness rather than judgement.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Bee-height scale is essential. Foreground petals wipe past close enough to feel huge; midground flowers hold pollen targets; background stems sway in warm daylight. Depth carries comedy: Fuzzby enters from one plane too fast, overshoots into another, and the leaf’s bend proves his weight. As thunder arrives, the background sky darkens through gaps above the flowers so the environment quietly changes before the characters finish processing it.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm begins as a bright work-song: Fuzzby’s “BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…” rides manic motion while Zenny’s calm work sets the tempo he cannot keep. Each gag escalates in physical consequence: leaf bounce, pollen moustache, smear worsening, tumble into blossom. Thunder then cuts the rhythm in half; the final boast tries to restart the parade but ends stuck again, proving the old rhythm can no longer protect him.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by speed, impact, revelation, or Zenny’s changed judgement. We do not cut mechanically from action to consequence to reaction; we cut when the scene changes ownership. Fuzzby earns traveling continuity during full-body cause-and-effect gags, but Zenny earns held punctuation when her stillness is the joke. The thunder transition earns a slower hold because the world has introduced new information.
treatments.openingImage: At bee height inside towering warm flowers, Zenny glides in a clean, efficient line through drifting pollen while Fuzzby rockets across the same space on a wild vertical zig-zag, already pitched into travel, pollen sacks bouncing like tiny alarm bells.
treatments.closingImage: Under slightly dimmed rainforest light, Fuzzby hangs newly stuck in a blossom after declaring he works well under pressure, chest still trying to be proud while his body is plainly trapped; Zenny hovers nearby, small and still, looking past him toward the storm-dark sky.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a safe flower-field master with bees performing inside it. The camera must be physically implicated in Fuzzby’s speed and must have the courage to lose him, find him, and then abandon him for Zenny. The danger is decorative chaos; the solution is readable physics: every leaf bend, pollen burst, and frame-edge escape must clarify cause, not become visual noise.

treatments.name: Zenny’s Perfect Workday Gets Fuzzbyed
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience experiences the meadow first as calm competence, then as a perfect little system repeatedly interrupted by a bee who believes interruption is leadership. Kids laugh because the neat world keeps getting messed up; adults enjoy the affection under Zenny’s restraint and the recognisable patience of someone working beside lovable chaos.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene is governed by Zenny’s experience. Her goal is simple: collect pollen smoothly and efficiently. Fuzzby’s goal is to be seen as official. The emotional comedy lives in her choosing, again and again, not to squash his dignity even while accurately naming the madness. When the storm comes, her patient observation becomes necessary care.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: deadpan observation. Fuzzby generates chaos, but the laugh lands when Zenny measures it with almost no movement. Secondary mechanisms: concealment to revelation for the pollen moustache, and restraint to release for her eventual smile.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Zenny is not cold; she is precise. Her calm is active thought: she tracks pollen, registers Fuzzby’s trajectory, calculates whether intervention is needed, then chooses the smallest possible response. Her line “Yes Fuzzby Officially nuts!” lands as affectionate punctuation, not insult. Fuzzby plays every accident as if it was part of his credentials: proud straightening after the leaf, face-presenting after the pollen, panicked over-fixing while insisting on command. On thunder, Zenny’s eyes go upward before her body moves; Fuzzby’s hover goes crooked, then he covers with performance.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene begins with visual order: repeated flower forms, smooth Zenny paths, neat pollen collection. Fuzzby disrupts that order by crossing angles, breaking rhythm, and dragging pollen through the clean composition. The camera treats Zenny’s stillness as the anchor, not as passivity; Fuzzby’s motion repeatedly invades and disturbs her measured world.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera stays close to Zenny’s working intelligence. It notices Fuzzby because she notices him. Sometimes Fuzzby is only a blur, a rustle, a leaf recoil, or a sudden pollen cloud entering her calm field before we fully see him. When she chooses to look, the scene grants him attention; when she withholds a laugh, the camera holds with her long enough for children to feel the pause.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement is framed as intrusion into calm. Zenny glides, stops, assesses, resumes. Fuzzby never simply enters; he ricochets into the scene’s order and tries to stand proudly inside the mess he made. The key contrast is not fast versus slow alone, but unexamined speed versus chosen economy.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is organised around Zenny’s efficient route through the flowers. Foreground flowers pass in soft calm arcs; Fuzzby repeatedly detonates in middle or background planes before forcing his way into her attention. The leaf FWIP can happen partially behind a stem so the environment reports the crash before the character reappears. As clouds gather, the ordered depth compresses: flowers that felt elegant now feel like a dense maze holding storm shadows.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm starts measured and graceful, then gets interrupted at increasingly shorter intervals. Zenny’s pauses lengthen as Fuzzby’s evidence becomes harder to ignore: leaf bounce, pollen badge, worsening smear, upside-down blossom. The thunder beat is the first interruption not caused by Fuzzby, so Zenny’s stillness changes flavour from comic judgement to alert warning.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts follow Zenny’s attention, not Fuzzby’s itinerary. We cut to new information when her eyes tell us something has entered the system; we hold when her non-reaction is the joke. Fuzzby’s tumbles may be partly off-screen if the aftermath is funnier through Zenny’s witness. No automatic reset wide: once the meadow geography is honest, we remain inside her lived workspace.
treatments.openingImage: Zenny, bee-height among tall swaying flowers, completes a neat pollen pass with calm precision; behind her, out of rhythm with everything, Fuzzby streaks through the depth in a jagged blur, already humming “BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…” before the calm can protect itself.
treatments.closingImage: Zenny has stopped collecting. She hovers very still in the dimmed flower corridor, eyes lifted toward the storm, while Fuzzby remains comically lodged nearby after his pressure boast — funny in the foreground, danger arriving beyond him.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The risk in a Zenny-led version is becoming static or polite. Stillness must be an opinion, not a parked camera. Compose her calm so Fuzzby can violate it from unexpected depth, edges, and occlusions. Let the audience discover his chaos as Zenny does, but never flatten the scene into reaction coverage.

treatments.name: The Meadow Joins the Double Act
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels the rainforest as a playful machine that likes both bees: soft flowers, springy leaves, and pollen clouds participate in the comedy. Kids read a living obstacle course; adults read a gentle world that catches Fuzzby’s failures without cruelty, until thunder changes the rules.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view is the environment witnessing Fuzzby and Zenny. The meadow is not a neutral backdrop; it reflects the contrast between belonging and overperformance. Fuzzby’s need is visible because the world keeps catching him, dusting him, bouncing him back, and still letting him remain part of the workday.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: environmental participation. The leaf FWIPs, pollen crowns him, petals frame his ‘official’ moustache, branches guide the tumble, and a blossom holds him upside down. Secondary mechanism: anticipation to reversal, because each natural object first looks helpful or harmless, then becomes the exact comic consequence of his overcommitment.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby treats every environmental consequence as accreditation. A leaf bounce becomes proof of agility; pollen on his face becomes official decoration; a worsening smear becomes a maintenance issue; being trapped becomes a pressure test he insists he is passing. Zenny behaves as someone fluent in the meadow’s rules: she moves with the flowers, reads the breeze, and trusts what the environment tells her. Her smile arrives because the meadow has made Fuzzby’s denial too elaborately visible to ignore.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar is cause-and-effect through soft natural physics. Bodies matter because the world answers them. Tall flowers sway before impact, petals tremble after, pollen hangs as evidence, leaves recoil with spring memory. The camera values aftermath as much as collision: the comedy lives in the meadow displaying what Fuzzby refuses to admit.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera often lets the environment lead. It may drift with a swaying flower before Fuzzby blasts through, ride a pollen puff as it reveals his face, or find Zenny through gaps in stems after a crash has already happened. The camera is curious and tactile, close enough to feel pollen grains and leaf spring, but always clear enough that small viewers understand where the bees are.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: The flowers move gently, Zenny moves with them, and Fuzzby moves against them. His motion is not random; it is a repeated argument with the meadow’s rhythm. When thunder arrives, the whole environment changes movement first: swaying becomes uneasy, petals tighten, pollen drift slows under dampening air. Fuzzby keeps trying to perform the old bounce while the meadow is already warning Zenny.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is the main storytelling tool. Foreground petals conceal and reveal; middle-depth leaves catch impacts; background sky glimpses shift from warm to storm-grey. The scene should feel tall and layered, with bees truly small inside rainforest scale. The pollen moustache gag works as environmental evidence: a bright cloud clears, and the meadow has drawn the joke onto him.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm begins as a breezy natural cycle: sway, collect, drift. Fuzzby adds syncopation: zig, dip, FWIP, pride. Each environmental response becomes bigger and more elaborate until the tumble through branches and flowers feels like the meadow playing percussion. Thunder then replaces comic percussion with one low interruption; the final stuck image makes clear that the playful world has become a warning world.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by environmental changes: a leaf recoil, a pollen burst, a petal clamp, a sky flicker, a sudden stillness in the flowers. We do not cut merely because a line starts. Dialogue rides the physical evidence already in frame. Holds are used when the environment has not finished reporting the consequence, especially before Fuzzby covers it with pride.
treatments.openingImage: A warm rainforest flower towers like a soft bell above the grass; its pollen trembles in the breeze, then Zenny passes cleanly through the drift as Fuzzby’s manic hum rockets in from beyond the petals, bending the delicate world around him.
treatments.closingImage: A blossom gently but firmly holds Fuzzby in place after “Good thing I work well under pressure,” while the flower tops beyond him tilt under the first storm wind; Zenny is the only figure aligned with that change, still and listening.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not treat the rainforest as set dressing behind two bees. The meadow must author jokes through physics and depth. The challenge is to make flowers, leaves, pollen, and storm light perform without stealing character clarity. If the camera waits safely for Fuzzby to enter a clean frame, we lose the living-world premise; let the frame discover consequences through the environment itself.

treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience rides Fuzzby’s proud little bee-rollercoaster through a soft living meadow, laughing at each bonk while slowly noticing through Zenny’s stillness and the changing weather that the world has become bigger than his performance.
treatmentSelection.rationale:
Select Treatment 1 as the spine. It has the clearest story truth: Fuzzby is not ‘the clumsy one’; he is a tiny performer trying to turn bodily failure into dignity before anyone can feel sorry for him. That is specific, funny, and emotionally legible for both doors — kids get the speed and FWIP, adults get the status-saving cover. Zenny’s stillness is correctly treated as emotional authority, not passive reaction.

Fold in Treatment 3’s strongest invention: the meadow as a tactile comic partner. Flowers, leaves, pollen, and storm-light should report Fuzzby’s denial before he can. This gives the scene visual memory and makes Crystal Cove feel alive without making the environment the emotional lead. The meadow catches him, dusts him, rebounds him, then warns Zenny first when the tone turns.

Borrow from Treatment 2 only its attention to Zenny’s precise intelligence: she is not an audience insert, she is the bear who understands the meadow’s rules and sees Fuzzby without humiliating him. But the scene should not be governed primarily by Zenny’s workday; that would make Fuzzby’s Want feel like an interruption rather than the engine.

The selected approach gives the scene a clean energy curve: manic work-song movement, escalating physical evidence, restrained relational puncture, then thunder cutting the rhythm in half. It offers strong cinematic opportunity because the camera is implicated in Fuzzby’s speed, then allowed to stop with Zenny when the world changes. It is feasible because the gag logic is built from readable soft physics — leaf bend, pollen burst, petal hold, storm shadow — not spectacle for its own sake.

Rejected as sole governing treatment: ‘Zenny’s Perfect Workday Gets Fuzzbyed’ because, although emotionally smart, making Zenny’s attention the primary camera law risks over-organising the scene into intrusion/non-reaction patterns and could undercut Fuzzby’s embodied Want. Use its stillness discipline, not its full governing POV.

Rejected as sole governing treatment: ‘The Meadow Joins the Double Act’ because an environmental POV can dilute the relationship if allowed to become the scene’s heart. The meadow may author consequences, but Fuzzby and Zenny must author meaning.

beats.sourceScript: At bee height in the flower field, Zenny’s graceful work is contrasted with Fuzzby’s full-throttle pollen chaos. His first crash into the leaf becomes his self-declared success, establishing that his comedy is not clumsiness alone but proud denial after impact.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Tiny pollen sacks bounce on their back legs. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.whatChanges: The flower field shifts from graceful pollen work into Fuzzby’s self-appointed parade, and his first visible failure is instantly rebranded as success.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the change by overcommitting to speed and pride; the leaf supplies the physical truth he cannot talk over.

beats.actionOrChoice: Fuzzby hums through a wild zig-zag, dives low, scoops pollen, overdoes the turn, hits the leaf, rebounds, and chooses a proud straighten-up instead of admitting the crash.
beats.consequence: The leaf’s FWIP proves his weight, pollen work becomes a stunt, and his line turns the impact into a comic self-coronation rather than a setback.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: We leave with the rule of the scene established: Fuzzby’s body tells the truth first, then his pride rushes in half a beat late to rename it.

orderedEvents.text: Good thing I work well under pressure.

voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Growing stillness, eyes lifting before the words arrive.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Protective alertness; she has shifted the scene from play to weather.
voicePerformances.pace: Slow and economical, with weight on 'Storm' and a quiet forward pull on 'coming'.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Three simple steps; no flourish, no panic.
voicePerformances.pauses: A small held look before the line; no internal pause, because certainty has replaced speculation.
voicePerformances.breaths: Quiet breath in as her eyes lead upward; controlled exhale through the sentence.

voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Comic helplessness as the launch is stopped by the blossom hold, but vocally he tries to leave as a hero.

voicePerformances.breaths: Quick forced inhale before 'Good'; let the final word tighten a touch under the physical stop.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: He launches too fast and is immediately held by petals while the wings keep insisting.

showrunnerJudgement: Passes showrunner review. I tried to break it on the usual Crystal Bears failures — safe meadow coverage, action/consequence/reaction cutting, decorative chaos, Zenny reduced to reaction punctuation — but the scene still holds its governing experience. Fuzzby’s motion owns the first run, the meadow gives honest physical consequences, and Zenny’s stillness is used as comic and emotional authority rather than as generic cutaway coverage. The thunder turn is correctly treated as a change in scene ownership: the camera stops chasing performance and lets the world become larger than him.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard remains aligned with the selected treatment. It preserves the bee-height rollercoaster, Fuzzby’s proud denial after each impact, the escalation from leaf rebound to pollen-status to worse-smear tumble, and the crucial contrast with Zenny’s precise economy. Most importantly, the storm does not arrive as a random plot event; it interrupts the rhythm Fuzzby has been using to protect his pride. Zenny’s stillness changes meaning from amused judgement to alert reading of the sky, which matches the treatment’s central emotional shift. The closing image also keeps the right bittersweet-comic shape: Fuzzby still performing importance while physically contradicted, with Zenny looking past him toward the larger danger.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. The two-unit split is justified. S1.SH1 is a near-full 28-second warm-meadow gag chain with setup, escalation, and tumble payoff; S1.SH2 is a separate 12-second storm-turn unit. The combined 40 seconds cannot safely fit a single 30-second Seedance request, and the boundary is not arbitrary: it protects a real dramatic and visual grammar change from chase-comedy to widened weather stillness. No avoidable adjacent short-unit merge is available under the 30-second limit.
